opportunities.title: Engine.create_abbreviation()/create_hotkey() raise AttributeError: module 'autokey.model.helpers' has no attribute 'TriggerMode'
opportunities.summary:
`lib/autokey/scripting/engine.py`'s `create_abbreviation()` and `create_hotkey()` (both public scripting API methods) reference `autokey.model.helpers.TriggerMode`. That attribute doesn't exist -- an earlier refactor moved `TriggerMode` into its own module (`autokey.model.triggermode`) without updating these two call sites. Any script calling `engine.create_abbreviation()` or `engine.create_hotkey()` hits an `AttributeError`. `tests/test_service.py` has the same stale reference in its `create_script()` test helper, which is why `test_set_triggered_abbreviation_uses_typed_abbreviation` fails. This has been silently broken since the refactor -- it was only caught because CI has been failing at an earlier "Install dependencies" step (missing `libgirepository-2.0-dev`, see #1182) since well before this bug was introduced, so the test suite never actually ran. Fix: import `TriggerMode` from `autokey.model.triggermode` in both files, matching the pattern already used elsewhere (e.g. `lib/autokey/model/folder.py`, `tests/test_phrase.py`).
